mechanism_narrative: The consistent upward trend in RETAIL_REC over the last two weeks, moving from -13.3% to -9.7%, indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity that will continue to drive mobility higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite the recent upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The significant recent increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, now above baseline at 2.1%, suggests increased comfort with out-of-home activities, which will spill over into discretionary retail over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above 0% change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in the next two weeks following GROCERY_PHARM exceeding baseline.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines while RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to fall and PARKS mobility continues to rise.

failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decrease, but RETAIL_REC falls in the next week.

candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility rises by more than 5 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility continues its strong recovery, yet RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next four weeks.

failure_condition: Both GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT continue to rise, but RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks.

candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES change from t-1w to t-0w is less than 0.5 points
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility remains stable, but RETAIL_REC decreases in the next week.
